summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of tracheobronchomalacia, bronchopulmonary dysplasia, chronic bronchitis, asthma, and GERD was admitted due to increased secretions, dyspnea on exertion, chills, and chest pressure over three days. She was initially treated with IV ceftriaxone for possible tracheitis, but remained afebrile with normal white blood cell counts. Imaging showed no acute cardiopulmonary process. The clinical course suggested non-infectious tracheal inflammation, and antibiotics were discontinued. She responded well to nebulized acetylcysteine, ipratropium, and albuterol. Iron deficiency anemia was addressed with ferrous sulfate initiation. She improved clinically and was discharged home with mucus-controlling medications, iron supplementation, and follow-up plans with her primary care provider and pulmonologist.
problems: Acute tracheitis without mention of obstruction
Other diseases of trachea and bronchus
